data.name: Fravash
data.gender_notes: Fravash is used as a neuter name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Fravash is derived from the ancient Persian and Avestan language, and holds significant meaning in Zoroastrianism. The name represents a guardian spirit or protector, believed to be present at birth and throughout one's life. Fravash offers spiritual guidance and protection, ensuring safety and well-being. The name Fravash carries the meaning “Protector Spirit” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Persian, Avestan. Parents who choose Fravash usually hope their child will grow to embody protector spirit and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Fravash is a symbol of the protective presence of the divine in one's life, providing spiritual guidance and protection.
data.etymology: Fravash belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Protector Spirit.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fravash total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_english.name: Fravash
in_english.long_meaning: Fravash is a Persian word meaning guardian spirit and protector, used in Islam to describe protective angels and the spirit that helps humans in life, derived from the Persian root fra meaning more or higher, and referenced in the Quran in the context of protection and guardianship

data.cultural_impact: In pre-Islamic Iranian culture, the belief in Fravashes as guardian spirits was widespread. Fravash was not only a personal protector but also a communal guardian. The Fravash Yasnas, a part of Zoroastrian scripture, were practiced to seek the blessings of these spirits.
data.spiritual_significance: Fravash is considered to be a watchful and guiding spirit who offers divine protection and spiritual guidance. It personifies the virtues of goodness, wisdom, and intelligence. Believers in Fravash ask for His blessings and invoke His name to ward off evil. The name Fravash is a reminder of the divine presence that protects and guides individuals throughout their lives.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Ibn al-Arabi, in his book 'Futuhat al-Makkiyya', described the Fravashis as being the guardian angels or spirits of the prophets and saints. He believed that every individual had a Fravashi, which was their personal guardian spirit and accompanied them throughout their lives.

The Fravashis were also mentioned in the Avestan texts of Zoroastrianism. In this context, they were described as the good Angels or Yazatas, who protected and guided the righteous and kept the evil at bay. This belief in the existence of these guardian spirits was prevalent in ancient Persia and influenced later religious thought in the region, including Islamic thought.
